lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary on a U.S.-style resume and can expose you to irrelevant bias.

items.says: Make sure the portfolio URL is clickable and leads directly to relevant, accessible case studies.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to see the work behind your strongest claims.

items.says: Use consistent formatting for locations, dates, separators, and capitalization.
items.because: Consistency makes scanning easier.

items.says: Consider adding relevant honors, coursework, or a distinction, if you have them.
items.because: They could strengthen your UX research profile.

items.says: Clarify the A/B test’s sample size and statistical reliability, if known.
Clarify which change contributed to the result.
items.because: The bullet combines shorter steps and saved progress.

items.says: Clarify whether the change from 37% to 22% is in percentage points or is a relative reduction.
A 3:1 contrast ratio is not sufficient for ordinary body text under WCAG AA.
items.because: The threshold is generally 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

items.says: Specify the text sizes and interface elements actually covered.
items.because: “Every background” is broad and may be difficult to substantiate.

items.says: Change “Synthesizing” to a past-tense opening verb.
items.because: The role has ended, and its bullets should describe completed work.

items.says: Make the sentence structure clear.
Specify what “repeat support calls” means.
Explain how the analysis connects to the 23% reduction.
items.because: That would make the causal claim credible.

items.says: Clarify whether 18 months is the period of tickets analyzed.
Explain what “the top five” refers to.
items.because: That would make the adoption result easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify how you know three fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
items.because: That would make the adoption result easier to assess.

items.says: Add the baseline or absolute number of tests behind “doubled,” if available.
items.because: That helps readers judge the scale of the result.

items.says: Clarify whether you supported the quality or governance of the tests.
items.because: More unmoderated research can raise questions about study rigor.

items.says: Add the number of people or sign-up volume behind the rates, if available.
items.because: That would make the change easier to evaluate.

items.says: Add a relevant measurement period or comparison, if available.
items.because: That would make the change easier to evaluate.

items.says: The stated calculation describes an average rating, not NPS.
items.because: NPS is not the average of 0–10 recommendation ratings.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period behind the increase.
Include the measurement period or number of appointments behind the missed-appointment rates, if available.
items.because: That would give the result more context.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The role has ended, and its bullets should describe completed work.

items.says: Say how many studies or what period the setup-time reduction was measured across, if available.
Clarify the age range meant by “older patients,” if relevant.
Clarify the measurement period behind the 30% reduction.
Keep “Present” only if you are still actively working on the transit map, and ensure the bullets reflect its current status.
Clarify what “redesigned” covered.
items.because: The line establishes the audience and testing, but not the scope of the work.

items.says: Clarify how the screen-reader and low-vision experience was evaluated.
The reduction from 90 to 60 seconds is 33%, not 50%.
Do not attribute the result to both design changes without distinguishing their contributions.
items.because: The bullet does not show which change mattered more.

items.says: The change from 65% to 85% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
Reduce the repetition of the previous bullet’s design changes.
items.because: The space could be used for a distinct finding.

items.says: Clarify the number of tasks or observations used to calculate the percentages.
items.because: 65% and 85% do not map neatly to whole participants out of 12.

items.says: Add the baseline volume or measurement period for the phone-booking change, if available.
Be cautious about implying the redesign alone caused the decline.
items.because: That attribution needs support.

items.says: Clarify the recruitment and testing setup.
items.because: “Hallway testing” suggests convenience recruitment, while “recruited 10 clinic patients” sounds like a defined patient sample.

items.says: Explain whether the six issues were all usability blockers or the issues you prioritized.
Clarify the handbook’s contribution to the later Spanish-language booking work.
items.because: It is unclear whether the teams used the handbook or the work simply happened afterward.

items.says: Correct the typo “interveiws.”
Review the skills list for coverage.
items.because: The experience shows a broader range of research and accessibility work than the list communicates.
